Yes. The subtext enriches the story naturally rather than feeling forced. Ilse’s “Ich muss nichts sehen” conveys practical familiarity with the river, but also suggests her reliance on routine amid uncertainty. Peters’s “Bloß nichts ändern” subtly reinforces the ferry’s role as an anchor of continuity for the community.

Most significantly, Ilse watches Jonas’s call go unanswered. His identity and their history remain unstated, yet her unusual act of releasing the rope signals emotional significance. Returning to her repetitive work suggests avoidance or retreat into familiarity. The fog, unseen shores, and recurring “Glied um Glied” give this emotional distance a physical setting without explicitly explaining it.
